content.text: Digital creators in regions where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable face a critical challenge: how to set up a robust crypto store that provides seamless payment processing and full ownership. In this analysis, we examine two COREMERCH deployment options—Stack 01 with GitHub Pages and Stack 02 with Cloudflare Pages—to determine which [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-selling-courses-without-teachable-stripe-6|COREMERCH guide to architecture]]-behind-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-without-stripe-what-actually-how-6|Selling Digital]]-ebooks-nigeria-without-paypal-4|architecture]] best meets your needs, especially in environments marked by financial restrictions.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Stack 01 utilizes GitHub Pages and Apps Script, offering a streamlined setup for those familiar with Git. It enables deployment in 4-6 hours using the Sovereign Blueprint, making it an attractive option for rapid implementation. However, it lacks the scalability features inherent in Stack 02. Conversely, Stack 02 leverages Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase, resulting in a more robust, end-to-end tested system deployed by COREMERCH in under 48 hours. This option is engineered to handle growth efficiently and supports more extensive product collections.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Both Stack 01 and Stack 02 are designed with creators in mind, particularly in regions facing financial isolation. Stack 01, by virtue of its simplicity, is accessible for creators who may not have extensive technical knowledge. It allows for quick setups in restricted countries. Stack 02, while requiring a bit more technical expertise, provides a more resilient architecture that can adapt to the varying needs of digital creators. It is engineered to handle potential regulatory and infrastructural challenges effectively, ensuring creators can operate with confidence.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Both stacks rely on NOWPayments for crypto payment processing, which charges a nominal 0.5% fee and allows for immediate payment verification. The payment speed is significantly faster compared to traditional platforms, providing instant on-chain confirmation. However, Stack 02's integration with Cloudflare Workers may offer enhanced performance due to its superior handling of backend logic, making it preferable for creators with higher transaction volumes. While Stack 01 is cost-effective for smaller operations, Stack 02 is built for scale without compromising on transaction efficiency.
Stack 01 is ideal for quick deployment but may limit your scalability.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

A critical differentiator between the two stacks is ownership and automation. With both options, creators retain full ownership of their infrastructure post-deployment, but Stack 02's advanced features such as automated order handling through Supabase streamline the delivery process. This means creators can focus on their products rather than logistics. Stack 01's manual processes may require more oversight, particularly as product offerings grow. For those prioritizing seamless delivery and automated systems, Stack 02 stands out as the superior choice.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you are new to digital commerce and need a quick setup with minimal technical barriers, Stack 01 could be the appropriate choice. However, if you anticipate growth and require a more robust solution, Stack 02 is the way to go. Its comprehensive features not only cater to immediate needs but also prepare your store for future scalability. Ultimately, the right choice hinges on your specific goals as a creator and your planned product range.

To build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free, Stack 01 is a straightforward option that can be deployed in as little as 4-6 hours. However, if you are looking for a more scalable solution with enhanced features, Stack 02 can be deployed in 48 hours and is designed for growth.

Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.
